story_text.value: Lovable for Photo Editing. Think of it like having an AI agent use photoshop in front of you. Just like with Lovable and vibe-coding, AI image editing is getting popular because it allows people to create beautiful edits of their photos without that specific domain expertise. However, the problem with AI image editing approaches right now is that they regenerate the photo. This approach is prone to mistakes such as the image generation model adding or removing certain details, or introducing diffusion noise. And since it “edits” by regenerating the whole photo, it leaves little control for the user to tweak certain image editing parameters themselves. It is not a true edit. PixlPal believes that AI should instead use deterministic tools (like in photoshop) to truly edit the images directly. So I created a custom Rust engine that exposes tools/APIs for an AI agent orchestrator to edit photos. The coolest part: I added a segmentation model that agents can call so it can select specific objects to apply specific transformations to as well.

story_text.value:
I'm having a really hard time working with claude. In the past when I wrote all the code manually, it was always carefully reviewed and architected, with all possible flows carefully mapped out. Now, my code is mostly AI written which has led to things going out of control. Since it's easy to add new features and support many user flows, we went ahead and implemented flows that support a lot of cases our users run into. But now, I feel like things are getting too complex with no central notion of behaviour definitions, which causes every bug-fixing session to feel like a game of whack-a-mole, and results in missing edge cases and UI bugs that are becoming impossible to review and keep track of.

Every time I build anything new, it adds more complexity and the agent only seems to focus on the surrounding code within that session without keeping track of how it fits into the rest of the code base/product.

How do you all deal with this? Any suggestions for improving?

title.value: How do you keep up quality when you vibe-code?

story_text.value:
Nobody writes the code any more. Agent do that. Nobody reads the code any more. Agent do that. Planning? what is it? 2020? Theres agents for that. Tickets? phhh, we have automated systems for that.

So your days usually are filled with bullshit tickets written by some agent automation that catches something that you would expect already be solved by this time.

You just forward the ticket to the coding agent, press enter couple of times, and post it for reviews in channels with other agent that listens to it, and review it on the git platform. you just shove any agent comments to the coding agent and tell it to push it once its done. You dont test your code, you just get ticket, enter, move one to next ticket.

I didnt imagined that this is what my life would look like.

title.value: Life as a Software Developer in 2026

story_text.value:
As a big TUI fan I've been complaining for a long time about not being able to read my Google Messages in a terminal. I wrote a client. It pairs with the Android phone, Google connection then emoji, the phone must remain on. The client manages SMS and RCS and groups, images (if you have a kitty compatible terminal), reactions, archives, spam, trash, searches, notifications...

Google Messages having no public interface, I wrote a specification https://github.com/louisrubet/gmessages-tui/tree/main/doc/pr... from the protocol decoded by mautrix-gmessages https://github.com/mautrix/gmessages in libgm https://github.com/mautrix/gmessages/tree/main/pkg/libgm. Thanks to you guys! This allowed me to write gmessages-proto, a clean-room client crate in Rust and a separated interface https://github.com/louisrubet/chat-tui-core I am reusing for another messenger. Messages are stored in a local encrypted database, whose key is stored in the system keystore.

Installation through cargo is `cargo install --locked gmessages-tui`.

There are deb, rpm and pacman packages if you prefer.

Tested on Linux only, please dare to install it on macOS or Windows, and open GitHub tickets!

story_text.value:
Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS.highlights` for text range highlighting without <span>s everywhere, `<dialog>` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0])

Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent <div>+JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge.

200+ guides (~1.7MB) of curated, hand-crafted implementation best-practices from web experts, updated as the web evolves. (Open source, obv, so.. we'll welcome your bikeshedding ;) Readable versions here: [1]

I've spent the last 9 months obsessing over how to ship this as an agent skill + (Agentic RAG) CLI without blowing up your context window. (Or cedeing activation mechanics to MCP dynamic tool search). The skill description is minmaxed for activating on relevant frontend tasks. The RAG work I'm pretty proud of… originally a 500mb native stack down to a ~7MB pure-JS package, ~10ms search on your CPU.

We just introduced a deterministic 'legacy-scan' (trained on 30k github repos) to identify old 'n dusted patterns that your agent can modernize. (92% avg precision on held-out repos.)

People make a lot of claims about what coding agents are good/bad at. We wanted receipts, so we invested heavily in eval infra [2] to help us hill-climb, but also to identify when knowledge is common enough we can prune our guides. (Ofc, some of the things we thought AI didn't know turned out to be wrong :) We run codex/claude/agy against 200 tasks without the skill and then with.. In total ~1,700 playwright/AST-based assertions. Agents go from 55% pass unguided to 92% guided.

Try it out:

    DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest install
    DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate dialog modal"
    DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan ./src
If you spot something wrong or weird, give us a holler!

Longer write-up on the 1.0: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1

---
